cards.text: Moses is still preaching to Israel before they go into the land God is giving them. Law after law, he's laying out how they're going to live there, and friend, this man has NOT run out of laws. Now he gets to marriage: if a man finds some indecency in his wife, he may write her a certificate of divorce, hand it to her and send her away.
Now say she leaves and becomes another man's wife. Then that second husband divorces her too, or he dies.

cards.question: True or false: if a divorced woman remarries and that second marriage ends, her first husband may marry her again.

cards.text: Next up, newlyweds. For one year, a newly married man must not be sent to war or pressed into any duty.

cards.question: A newlywed gets a whole year with no war and no duty. What is he free to do with it?

answers.text: Stay home and bring joy to his wife
Serve the priests at the tabernacle
Build a new house for his family

cards.text: The closest I ever got to a year off was the junk drawer, and NOBODY was bringing anybody joy in there. Next, loans: a lender must not take a pair of millstones, or even just the upper one, as security for a debt.

cards.question: Why can't a lender take a man's millstones as security for a debt?

answers.text: It would take his livelihood as security
Millstones belong to the whole town
They are too heavy to carry off

cards.question: Then Moses gets serious. If a man kidnaps a fellow Israelite and treats him as a slave or sells him, the kidnapper must ___.

cards.text: Then Moses turns to infectious skin diseases. He tells Israel to be careful to follow everything the people in charge of those cases instruct them.

cards.question: In cases of infectious skin disease, whose instructions does Moses tell Israel to follow?

answers.text: The elders at the city gate

cards.text: And Moses adds a reminder: remember what the LORD did to Miriam on the journey out of Egypt. Miriam, Moses' sister, was struck with a skin disease on that road (Numbers 12:10; 26:59).
Back to loans. Say you lend your neighbor something, and now it's time to collect the security.

cards.question: When a lender comes to collect security from his neighbor, what does Moses say he must do?

answers.text: Stand outside while it's brought out
Go inside and pick what he wants
Bring two witnesses in with him

cards.text: And if the borrower is a poor man, the lender must not go to sleep with his security still in hand.

cards.question: The lender is to return the poor man's security by ___, so he may sleep in his own cloak and bless him.
True or false: Moses says giving the poor man's security back will be credited as righteousness before the LORD.

cards.text: Moses keeps going, and now it's payday. Do not oppress a hired hand who is poor and needy, whether he's an Israelite or a foreigner living in your towns.

cards.question: Moses says to pay a poor hired hand his wages each day before ___.
Why does Moses say a poor hired hand's pay can't wait?

answers.text: He is poor and depends on it
He might leave for another town

cards.text: Hold it back, and he may cry out to the LORD against you, and you'll be guilty of sin. So not "the check's in the mail," not "next Friday," friend, it's TODAY, TODAY, TODAY!

cards.question: Then Moses talks about who is put to death for whose sin. True or false: children can be put to death for their fathers' sins.

cards.text: Moses says do not deny justice to the foreigner or the fatherless. And do not take a widow's cloak as security.

cards.question: What reason does Moses give Israel for treating the foreigner, the fatherless and the widow this way?

answers.text: They were once slaves in Egypt
Foreigners bring trade to their towns
Widows can take them to the elders

cards.text: Harvest time, and you forget a sheaf out in the field. Friend, I once hunted an hour for my spatula, and it was in my MUSTACHE, I was HOLDING it.

cards.question: At harvest, a farmer forgets a sheaf out in his field. What does Moses say he should do about it?

answers.text: Leave it behind for those in need
Go back for it before nightfall
Bring it to the priests as an offering

cards.question: Leave the forgotten sheaf, so the LORD your God may ___ you in all the work of your hands.
True or false: when Israel harvests olives and grapes, they must not go over the branches or the vines a second time, so what remains is left for the foreigner, the fatherless and the widow.

cards.text: And Moses brings back that reminder: remember you were slaves in the land of Egypt. That's why he's commanding all this.
Next, the courtroom. Disputes go before a judge, and if the guilty man deserves a beating, he gets the number of lashes his crime warrants, but no more than forty.

cards.question: Why does Moses cap a guilty man's beating at forty lashes?

answers.text: So the guilty man isn't humiliated
So the judge can hear more cases
So the punishment ends by sunset

cards.question: Then Moses talks about an ox treading out the grain. What does he say not to do to it?

answers.text: Let it eat the grain it treads
Work it after the sun goes down

cards.text: Working right next to a snack and can't have a bite? That's me beside a fresh tray of cookies, not allowed to sneak ONE. Now a family law: when brothers live together and one dies without a son, his brother is to marry the widow.

cards.question: The first son the widow bears will carry on the name of the ___ brother.

cards.text: But what if the brother doesn't want to marry his brother's widow? Moses has that covered too.

cards.question: True or false: if the brother refuses, the widow takes it to the elders at the city gate.
The elders summon the brother, and he still says he doesn't want to marry her. In front of the elders, the widow takes something off him. What is it?

cards.text: A sandal! Friend, I don't even have feet, I have a gold base, and NOBODY is taking my base. Then she spits in his face and declares, “This is what is done to the man who will not maintain his brother’s line.”

cards.question: From then on, his family name in Israel will be known as the House of the ___.

cards.text: Then a law about a fight. If a wife tries to rescue her husband by grabbing the attacker's genitals, her hand is to be cut off, with no pity shown.

Then business: no two differing weights in your bag, one heavy and one light, and no two differing measures in your house. Friend, if I had two scoops, my mustache would be holding BOTH, and I'd STILL grab the wrong one.

cards.question: Moses says Israel must keep accurate and honest weights and measures. Why?

answers.text: So they may live long in the land
So the priests get a fair tithe
So the king can tax them fairly

cards.question: True or false: Moses says everyone who is dishonest with weights and measures is detestable to the LORD.

cards.text: Then Moses brings up the Amalekites, who attacked Israel at Rephidim (Exodus 17:8). They met Israel on the journey from Egypt, when everyone was tired and weary.

cards.question: Israel is tired and weary on the road. Who do the Amalekites attack?
True or false: Moses says once the LORD gives Israel rest from their enemies, they can forget what Amalek did.

cards.text: Instead, Moses says to blot out the memory of Amalek from under heaven. And friend, Moses is NOT done preaching yet, so keep that oven warm.
